claim: Two-step shikimate→DHS→protocatechuate route uses QuiA then QuiC. QuiB is the quinate branch; no DHQ intermediate is inserted into shikimate degradation I.

ADP1/BD413 growth genetics and native extracts support QuiA. Published enzyme assay uses quinate/DCIP; do not call this purified ADP1 shikimate kinetics. E. coli DH5α (pZR504) standard activity remained undetectable even with 12 nM PQQ.
Five N-terminal transmembrane segments and PQQ-family features are sequence inference, not direct topology or purified ADP1 cofactor measurement.

locator: Methods, p. 5972; cloning results and Table 1, p. 5973; mutant results, pp. 5974–5975
claim: pZR564 quiC insert expressed in E. coli DH5α extracts converts DHS to PCA; pZR571 truncation loses activity. ADP629 quiB deletion grows on shikimate, unlike quiC-defective/polar mutants. Numeric units and native DHQ typo are not copied.
QuiX function is not established by porin homology; mutant grows like wild type at 5 mM shikimate. No transport edge.

locator: Author reprint: Methods, p. 83; Table 1 and paragraph above it, p. 85; Discussion, p. 89
claim: Table 1 records shikimate growth of LMD 79.41 and impaired growth of PQQ-biosynthesis mutants. The paragraph above the table reports rescue by 1 µM PQQ; Methods identifies the historical isolate as A. calcoaceticus using API 20 NE. Retain NCBITaxon:471 source context separately from ADP1, without claiming modern strain retyping or a sequenced catalyst.

Quinate/Wurster’s Blue extract assays, PQQ rescue and particle association; no solubilization/purification attempted. Periplasm is expressly assumed; unidentified metal requirement inferred from EDTA. No ADP1 purified assay, calcium-specific or periplasm edge.

Purified Acinetobacter sp. SA1 holo-QDH/Acinetobacter calcoaceticus AC3 apo-QDH show shikimate turnover and DHS product; shikimate Km of 0.26 mM and 74% of the quinate rate must not transfer to ADP1/Gluconobacter. Q2 acceptance concerns quinate oxidation, not a demonstrated shikimate/Q2 paired assay.

IFO3244 soluble/cytoplasmic fraction DHS-dehydratase is partially separated at 0.225 M KCl; PCA assay is qualitative. No sequence/oligomer inferred; NADPH belongs to analytical/biosynthetic SKDH, not DHS-dehydratase cofactor.
Inspected abstract supports membrane holo-QDH and PQQ with possible proteolysis into 65 and 21 kDa bands. It does not itself establish shikimate turnover or complete same-strain degradation route.

Addition of 2 mM protocatechuate to ADP1 growing on 20 mM pyruvate raises Northern signals after 15 min. In ADP331, the 552 bp pcaU deletion abolishes inducer dependence. The 442 bp quiA probe measures 25% of the induced wild-type signal; the shared 1,522 bp quiC–quiX probe measures 14% and supports quiC at the operon level. These are expression effects inferred from genetic perturbation, not direct enzyme activation or ligand-binding assays.

Most induced quiA transcription depends on pcaIp; constitutive quiAp remains independent of PcaU/PCA. A full 14.4 kb transcript was inferred, not directly detected. No invented physical promoter/transcript ID; no universal shutoff claim.
Periplasmic QuiC/QuiB location is discussed using older predictions; authors acknowledge unresolved separation. No experimentally proven QuiC periplasm edge.
